analysis.title: Energy risks take a step back
key_insights: Risk appetite improved as Trump played down the prospect of immediate military action against Iran, unwinding part of the geopolitical risk premium. Oil fell sharply to $94, pulling European gas prices and inflation expectations lower.
Equities rebounded strongly and government bond yields fell. Natixis cautions that uncertainty around the conflict and energy supplies remains significant.
Euro area October flash headline inflation rose to 4.0% from 3.8%, driven by energy. Core was unchanged at 2.5%, suggesting limited spillover from the energy shock into underlying prices.
Headline inflation supports expectations of another ECB rate hike in December. Stable core inflation argues against a more aggressive tightening path.

Natixis expects the Bank of England to hike 25bp today, citing persistent services inflation, resilient activity and a modest recovery in private-sector wage growth. Base case is a further hike in February 2027.
EUR and US rates eased sharply on lower energy prices. The 10-year Bund fell 6bp to 3.27%, the 2-year Schatz fell 6bp to 3.00%, and the 10-year UST fell nearly 4bp to 4.85%.
Peripheral and French bonds outperformed Bunds. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread narrowed nearly 12bp to 150bp.
Natixis owns a 6m forward 2s10s conditional bull steepener.
DXY fell 0.29% to 101.58, its largest daily decline in three weeks, and USD/CHF fell 0.50% to 0.8165. EUR/USD rose 0.20% to 1.1215, the euro's highest level in nearly a month.
The Stoxx Europe 600 rose 1.8%, its biggest one-day gain since June, to within half a percentage point of its all-time high. Banks, luxury and renewables led.

The S&P 500 had its best session in three months. Mega-cap tech led on bets that a Democrat-controlled Congress will curb AI capex, freeing up cash flow. Semiconductors and data center stocks lagged, and health care outperformed on expected Medicaid subsidy expansion.
Credit tightened sharply: iTraxx Main -3.8bp, Crossover -17bp, CDX NA IG -2.5bp. French credits and airlines (Lufthansa, IAG, 5-year CDS tighter by 8 to 10bp) outperformed.
Meta issued its first euro bond: €9bn across six tranches of 8 to 38 years, with a €53bn order book. BMW spreads widened about 3bp after a profit warning.
UK composite PMI rose for a fourth month to 52.9 in October, the highest since February. French final services PMI was revised down to 46.2 from a 48.4 flash estimate.

ECB wage tracker rises from 2.6% in 2026 to 2.8% in the first three quarters of 2027, excluding one-off payments. US ISM services slipped to 54.5, its slowest pace in three months, with new orders at a four-month low.
CM Arkéa suffered a contained cyberattack with possible fraudulent flows above €100m. Natixis expects no material credit impact.

Deutsche Telekom raised full-year guidance to about €47.6bn adjusted EBITDAaL and €20.1bn FCF after leases, mainly on higher T-Mobile US expectations. SES lowered 2026 capex to about €600mn from €700mn.
earnings_insights: Deutsche Telekom Q3 reported adjusted EBITDAaL €12.21bn (+9.9% YoY) and revenue €31.10bn, both above expectations. Full-year guidance raised to about €47.6bn adjusted EBITDAaL and about €20.1bn FCF after leases.

SES 9M 2026 reported revenue €2,472mn (+41.8% reported, -2.0% like-for-like at constant FX) and adjusted EBITDA €1,138m (45.8% margin), with Intelsat fully consolidated. 2026 outlook reiterated, capex now about €600mn (previously €700mn).

tension_points.bull_case: Easing Iran tensions cut Brent to $94, lowering gas prices and inflation expectations, which drove an equity rebound and lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Uncertainty around the conflict and its implications for energy supplies remains significant, so the improvement should be treated with caution.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed escalation or military action against Iran that reverses the oil decline.
